articles.headline: Intel Unveils D‑Series GPUs for AI Inference
articles.dek: Intel announced a new D‑Series GPU line tailored for AI inference, with up to 480 GB of memory per device.

body.text: Key Takeaway
Intel’s D‑Series GPUs target AI inference and pack up to 480 GB of memory, a head‑count shift for anyone serving large models [FACT:dfa259d52d6c3b9d49811278acd7582f].
Why This Matters
More on‑board memory lets model‑comparison pipelines keep bigger models resident, cutting data‑movement latency and inference cost [FACT:dfa259d52d6c3b9d49811278acd7582f].
What Happened
At a recent industry summit, Intel revealed the D‑Series lineup and positioned the family as inference‑only accelerators rather than general‑purpose GPUs [FACT:18c86e2098d63f8eb13a177440c9ee18].
Builder View

If you’re currently using consumer GPUs for serving, the D‑Series offers a purpose‑built roof for inference workloads, so you can start planning migration or hybrid deployments once silicon ships [FACT:18c86e2098d63f8eb13a177440c9ee18].
Open Questions

Intel has not yet published performance metrics, driver timelines, or pricing, so teams should monitor upcoming technical briefs before budgeting for hardware upgrades [FACT:18c86e2098d63f8eb13a177440c9ee18].
Ardur Take

The announcement comes from a single source but includes a concrete 480 GB memory figure; treat the D‑Series as a signal to prototype when official availability is confirmed [FACT:dfa259d52d6c3b9d49811278acd7582f].

keyPoints: Intel introduced D‑Series GPUs aimed at AI inference.
Top SKU provides up to 480 GB of on‑board memory.
Announcement is single‑source; details may evolve.
